newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns BB-plus to PLDT global bonds.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns BB-plus to PLDT global bonds.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp has assigned a BB-plus rating to both tranches of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co's (PLDT) US$500 million global bond issue, the rating agency said on Wednesday.
PLDT has issued US$200 million 7.85 percent bonds maturing on March 6, 2007, and US$300 million 8.35 percent bonds maturing on March 6, 2017.
S&P said the company's rating outlook is positive.
S&P raised the long-term foreign currency rating of PLDT to BB-plus from BB on February 21 following its upgrade of the Republic of the Philippines to BB-plus from BB.
Despite increasing competition, S&P expects PLDT to remain the dominant telecommunications provider in the Philippines for at least the medium term.
Increased use of debt to finance continuing network expansion and modernisation is expected to lead to further deterioration in PLDT's financial position, S&P said.
Because PLDT is a net importer of international calls, pressures to reduce international accounting rates also will adversely affect the company's financials, S&P said.
However, S&P said PLDT's finances are expected to remain reasonably strong.
PLDT's finances will be bolstered somewhat if the government allows the company to introduce a greater level of cost-based pricing for local telephone services, S&P said.
